jobs.title: Director of Technical Program Management, Space Radar
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Space team is at the forefront of advancing national security capabilities in the space domain. Our mission is twofold: 1) develop autonomous satellite systems and space-based platforms, and 2) deliver critical ground and orbital software infrastructure at scale. We transform products and capabilities across space command and control (C2), mission management, and space operations from early concepts into fully operational systems by partnering closely with specialist engineering, operations, and production teams. Through our integrated approach, we design and deploy space software systems using advanced algorithms, distributed architectures, and resilient infrastructure—delivering reliable, mission-critical capabilities that support operators across orbital and ground-based assets. Space Systems hires software engineers and systems engineers who are excited to build across a diverse and powerful portfolio—from satellite operations software to space domain awareness platforms. Our teams contribute to highly capable autonomous space systems and ground software products that operate reliably in the most demanding mission environments, supporting the DOD and IC in defending our national interests in space.

ABOUT THE JOB

We're seeking a Director of Technical Program Management to lead a flagship space-based radar program. You will own end-to-end execution of this massive initiative spanning radar payload development, spacecraft integration, ground systems, and mission operations. This role demands deep technical fluency in radar systems and algorithms combined with the ability to drive large-scale program execution, manage executive-level customer relationships, and coordinate across hardware, software, and operations teams. You'll be the central figure ensuring this critical program delivers on time, on budget, and exceeds mission requirements.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Own program execution including schedule, budget, risk management, and delivery across all phases from development through launch and on-orbit operations

- Serve as primary technical and programmatic interface with government customer, leading executive-level reviews, milestone demonstrations, and strategic planning

- Drive technical decision-making across radar architecture, algorithm development, antenna development, spacecraft integration, and ground systems ensuring sound engineering trades and system performance

- Coordinate cross-functional execution across radar engineering, antenna, software, spacecraft, mission operations, production, and test teams

- Build and lead a high-performing program management team and establish scalable processes for execution at program scale

- Translate customer mission needs into engineering requirements and program plans, working closely with the Head of Radar Engineering and technical leads

- Lead systems engineering processes including requirements management, interface control, V&V, and technical risk mitigation

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in an Engineering discipline (e.g., Aerospace, Electrical, Mechanical, Computer Science, Systems Engineering)

- Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with a proven ability to distill complex technical concepts, risks, and status into clear, actionable insights for both deeply technical and executive audiences

- Experience with the deployment and integration of sophisticated hardware and software systems - particularly for national security space systems

- Experience with building and leading cross-functional teams

- Experience serving DoD/IC customers and comfortable interfacing with key government stakeholders on a frequent basis

- Adaptive and introspective; willing to learn, teach, lead and follow

- Comfortable with setting and achieving goals in an amorphous environment

- Comfortable with working in limited resource environments

- Prior engineering work on space systems or missile defense systems is a plus

- Ability to travel up multiples times per quarter based on program needs

- Active U.S. Top Secret or TS/SCI clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Direct experience with space-based radar, SAR, GMTI, or RF sensing payload programs

- Background in radar algorithm development, signal processing implementation, or real-time processing architectures

- Hands-on engineering experience in radar systems or space systems prior to program management

- Experience with DoD/IC acquisition processes and earned value management

- Experience managing programs through launch campaigns and on-orbit operations

- Prior systems engineering role on satellite payloads or complex defense systems

- Experience with NewSpace development approaches and rapid iteration

US Salary Range
$220,000 — $292,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. - Proven ability to operate as a trusted peer to engineering leadership.

- Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret test data, diagnose system behaviors, and recommend actionable improvements

- Organized and detail-oriented, with strong verbal & written communication skills

- Proven track record of working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to achieve project milestones and deliverables

- Ability to leverage operational experience and technical knowledge to make educated decisions and leverage engineering trades in the absence of clear customer requirements

- Direct experience in the development, testing, and deployment of mission autonomy systems in a defense or aerospace context

- Familiarity with agile software development practices

- Knowledge of current industry and military standards related to unmanned aerial systems and their operation within national airspace

- Familiarity with the principles of mission autonomy, unmanned systems, and the integration of multiple assets into cohesive operational frameworks

- Collaborative Support: Continue supporting broader operational goals, including demand planning, hardware/software integration, and internal partnership development.

- Broader Scope: Where applicable, lend expertise to other product lines that overlap with the functionalities of the Voyager platform.

- Ability to take fragmented signals from multiple functions and assemble them into a clear picture for leadership

- Prior experience succeeding in influence-based roles driving outcomes through persistence and relationships rather than org chart leverage

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. security clearance

Anduril runs on trusted data, and today too much of it means different things to different teams. At a time when air superiority can no longer be taken for granted, the Air Defense team provides mission-critical capabilities to warfighters. From detection to tracking, identification, deterrence, and defeat, our family of networked sensors and effectors enables our customers to rapidly close the kill chain against a broad range of uncrewed aerial system (UAS) threats. Working across product, engineering, business development, logistics, operations, and mission success, the Air Defense team develops, tests, deploys, and sustains the Anduril Air Defense Family of Systems in challenging operational environments worldwide.

Within Air Defense, the Command & Control (C2) team owns the compute and infrastructure backbone that fuses those sensors and effectors into a single, coherent air defense picture. This role is the operational connective tissue between the field, product, and engineering for that compute.

ROLE SPECIFICS

Working closely with senior team members, you'll maintain our systems of record, execute and improve process and tooling, and contribute to the feedback loop that turns field failures, readiness signals, and deployment friction into structured, prioritized insight for engineering, product, and program stakeholders.

You'll partner with product, engineering, program management, deployment operations, and sustainment to translate what's happening in the field into action. If you enjoy building order out of ambiguity, love turning messy operational data into decisions, and are passionate about supporting national security priorities through cutting-edge technology, we'd like to hear from you.

- 2+ years of experience in product operations, technical operations, program/product support, or a comparable role in a high-energy, fast-paced startup, hardware, or logistics environment

- Demonstrated ability to turn operational or field data into insights and recommendations that support cross-functional decisions

- Ability to communicate and coordinate technical and non-technical efforts across product, engineering, business, and sustainment functions

- Ability to work proficiently and stay organized across multiple connected systems (e.g., Oracle ERP, Odoo, Salesforce, JIRA, Slack)

As part of this team, your role will involve building the Product Operations function within a larger deployment and sustainment group. ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Product Operations Technical Specialist for Maritime, you will play an important role in ensuring the reliability and readiness of Anduril’s Maritime products. This family of intelligent, autonomous undersea systems work together to develop unmatched situational awareness, precision engagement, and scalable maritime dominance. You will be an integral piece to ensuring that Anduril meets this mission for our customers. In this role you will help support end users by following and improving field failure discovery, mitigation, and resolution processes. You will help identify failure modes that contribute to root cause analysis, and you will help deploy fixes and manage the incident lifecycle across the Maritime fleet. This position requires a strong problem-solving mindset and hands-on expertise in debugging and resolving complex electromechanical issues. If you are passionate about cutting-edge technology, advancing national security, and delivering best-in-class operational support, Anduril invites you to join the team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Own Incident Triage and Resolution: Be the first technical responder for issues across our global Maritime fleet. Dig into logs, telemetry, and system state to isolate faults across software, hardware, and network boundaries, and drive incidents to resolution.

- Keep Customers Operational: When a full engineering fix will take time, identify and deploy interim mitigations and workarounds so customers can keep operating, while you manage the permanent fix in parallel.

- Analyze Fleet Telemetry: Pull, query, and analyze fleet health data and logs yourself to spot trends, predict failures, and prevent issues before they reach the customer.

- Drive Fleet Reliability: Partner directly with software and hardware engineering teams to turn real-world field data and failure analysis into permanent system upgrades and design improvements.

- Bridge the Gap: Act as the critical translator between deeply technical engineering teams, business development stakeholders, and military operators in the field, explaining complex issues clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Help Build the Playbook: Turn what you learn on real incidents into repeatable triage procedures, diagnostic tooling, and runbooks that scale as the Maritime fleet grows worldwide.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, OR equivalent hands-on technical experience (military, maritime, industrial, or field support).

- Systems Troubleshooting: Hands-on experience troubleshooting software-intensive or networked systems in a production, field, or customer-facing environment (for example: reading logs, isolating faults across software and hardware boundaries, reproducing issues).

- Command Line and Data Skills: Working proficiency with the Linux command line, and comfort analyzing data beyond spreadsheets (SQL, Python, bash, or similar).

- Problem-Solving Mindset: A proven ability to work through ambiguous, unstructured technical problems from first principles, including the instinct to deploy interim mitigations and workarounds that keep customers operational while permanent fixes are engineered.

- Self-Driven: Self-starter with a record of high achievement in multiple domains, who learns new systems by getting hands-on with them.

- Technical Communication and Collaboration: Ability to communicate and coordinate technical and non-technical efforts across business, engineering, and sustainment functions, influencing decision-making, resource allocation, and operational planning.

- Clearance and Location: Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance, and based in (or willing to relocate to) Quincy, MA.

- Travel and Schedule: Ability to travel as needed to support customer operations and test events. Willingness to work non-standard hours and weekends as needed.

We recognize that great leaders come from diverse backgrounds. We do not expect you to meet every single one of these criteria:

- Prior experience in a technical support escalation, field service engineering, site reliability (SRE), or customer-facing technical operations role.

- Scripting experience (Python or bash) used to automate diagnostics, parse logs, or build internal tooling.

- Familiarity with modern observability and ticketing tools (such as Grafana, Jira, or Git).

- Experience with data platforms (such as Palantir Foundry) to conduct trend analysis and drive decisions.

- Experience supporting and/or deploying undersea munitions, vehicles, or unmanned undersea systems (UUVs) as a DoD contractor or military end-user.

- Familiarity with naval systems or operations, or prior military, DoD civilian, or government agency experience.

Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. ABOUT THE TEAM

Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build and deploy the technology stack that powers Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, the manufacturing execution system that workers and planners use every shift, the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that remove manual toil from the shop floor and business operations. MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology, incubating solutions close to the production line, validating them with real operators, hardening them for reliability and security, and scaling them across sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship. MDP is scaling from a founding team to more than 70 engineers across multiple U.S. sites, and you will be joining early to shape how manufacturing software is built at Anduril.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Senior Product Manager for Manufacturing Software, you will own the product strategy, roadmap, and success metrics for the factory floor applications that production operators, supervisors, and manufacturing engineers rely on every shift. You will own the deployment of these products onto the factory floor, working shoulder to shoulder with the people who build ships to make sure the software earns its place in their workflow.
Product Strategy
You can “see around the corner” for your product, crafting the vision, high-level roadmap, and critical dependencies for 6 to 12 months into the future. You constantly engage with stakeholders to solicit input and buy-in, proactively communicating product goals and managing expectations for delivery. You escalate large tradeoffs and decision points as needed. You work effectively across many internal teams to synthesize their needs, but are never afraid to make important decisions as the owner of your product.
Product Prioritization
You work backward from your strategy to set clear outcomes for your portfolio in partnership with your engineering, design, and operations partners. You support team structures that allow prioritization of competing work within rapid development cycles, and you let your team flex to adapt goals when new information arrives.
Problem Discovery and Solution Generation
You become attached to problems, not solutions. You seek out real-world context through onsite user research on the factory floor, direct conversations with technicians and operators, internal expert feedback, existing product data, and industry investigation. You separate what a customer asks for from what a customer actually needs, capture core workflows, and translate them into well-scoped requirements and success hypotheses.
Product Execution
From design to delivery, you fill gaps wherever needed to make your well-scoped solutions a reality. You proactively communicate with internal team members and stakeholders, approach solutions with humility and creativity to hit milestones, and set a high bar for the product you own, including how it is deployed, adopted, and supported on the floor.

- Communicating across stakeholders and interested parties on roadmap and delivery, and exercising the judgment to tell whether a stakeholder truly needs what they are asking for or whether the underlying problem is better solved another way

- Walking the factory floor, talking directly with technicians and operators about how their work is going, and turning what you hear into opportunities to fix and improve the product

- Navigating the organizational dynamics between Maritime Digital Production and partner platform teams, advocating from the customer point of view when Maritime's needs differ from how a platform team would prefer to build

- Exploring and incorporating technologies that enhance Anduril's operational leverage

- Driving adoption and enablement of manufacturing software across production and operations teams

- 8+ years in a software product management role or similar leading role in product development

- Domain expertise within hardware-related industries such as manufacturing, supply chain, warehousing, or logistics

- Demonstrated ability to gather and refine both functional and non-functional requirements (such as capacity, performance, and reliability) and turn them into a prioritized backlog

- Strong understanding of the interplay between enterprise systems, including ERP, WMS, MES, PLM, and supplier portals

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work with stakeholders across a wide range of technical comfort and to judge whether a request reflects a real underlying need

- Demonstrated success working directly with end users in operational environments, including time spent on a production or factory floor observing workflows firsthand

- Ability to navigate cross-team and cross-department dynamics, representing the customer point of view and building alignment when priorities differ

- Ability to balance requirements across engineering, design, data, and business stakeholders

- Demonstrated success decomposing a problem into addressable component parts and arranging the correct sequencing

- Proven ability to “see around corners” by crafting product strategy for 6 to 12 months into the future

- Comfort maturing a product from MVP to enterprise-grade production

- Must be able to travel up to 25% of the time

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

- Experience with UI / UX web design tools (e.g. Figma)

- Narrative-Building : Possess a strong story-telling skillset and the ability to tailor that narrative across audiences (government stakeholders, other vendors, engineers, etc.). You'll make sure everyone on the team not only understands what we are building, but why as well.

- 5+ years relevant industry experience

- Recent experience managing DoD programs

- Operational background working with technically advanced systems requiring an understanding of complex software and hardware products.

- Proven experience working with multi-disciplinary engineering teams and customers

The Connected Warfare division builds cutting-edge technology spanning communications, networking, computing, and intelligent C2 software. Our mission is to foster strong relationships throughout our many Anduril teams to ensure that customer challenges are met with unified and innovative solutions.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager who excels at building and nurturing internal relationships. You will be the key liaison that connects diverse Anduril business lines to foster collaboration, drive mutual success, and enhance customer outcomes.

Orchestrate Internal Collaboration. Build and maintain strong working relationships across departments (engineering, product, supply chain, logistics, and growth). Facilitate clear communication and align strategic priorities to create a unified approach to customer missions.

Drive Customer Success through Partnership. Act as the internal advocate for customer needs by sharing feedback and insights with relevant teams. Collaborate with stakeholders to identify and capitalize on opportunities that benefit Anduril and our customers.

Enhance Product Deployment. Oversee the planning and execution of Anduril product deployments with seamless integration. Gather user feedback and work with engineering teams to refine offerings and meet mission requirements.

Foster a Culture of Teamwork. Serve as the central contact for bridging gaps between internal teams. Seek to deeply understand and represent partnership interests, driving initiatives that enhance internal synergy.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Mission First Mindset . We put the needs of the mission and our customers first and understand that the US and its allies have no preordained right to victory in any future conflict. We actively seek out opportunities to better understand our customers’ mission needs, with a goal to build the best possible products for the warfighter and radically evolve our national and international defense capabilities. We push ourselves and the limits of our capabilities in the pursuit of this goal.

Ownership Mentality. We’re looking for owners; those who have a natural bias to assume responsibility, a healthy dose of skepticism, and contribute to a culture of performance. We empower our Mission Operators to quickly assume high levels of responsibility and entrust them to actively own their account and shape its success. Our Mission Operators are just as comfortable helping to shape a proposal or pitch a new customer as they are working with engineers on new features or deploying products in the field.

Technical Aptitude and Intellectual Curiosity. We are first and foremost a technology company, working at the leading edge of capabilities like machine learning, autonomy, distributed networking, and multi-modal sensor fusion. Do you have a natural desire to see beyond simple cause and effect relationships to really understand how complex systems operate? Do you actively seek out opportunities to educate yourself? These capabilities form the foundation of our product offerings, so we are looking for those who are comfortable communicating technical concepts and can articulate them in the context of the customer’s mission.

Structured Thinker and Problem Solver. Leading technical programs requires clear communication and well thought-out plans. We are looking for assertive communicators who bring a thoughtful perspective and honest dialogue. A solution-driven approach, the ability to distill complexity into its essential, digestible components, and the ability to supervise execution are critical to ensure mission success.

High Value Team Member. Do you enjoy working as part of a team? At Anduril, the path to success weaves through the organization - account teams, engineering, logistics, technical operations, and more. It requires humility, an eagerness to learn, and empathy toward your fellow team member. We assume best intentions and empathize with customers just as we do with our colleagues. Can you develop rapport at both the user and executive levels? Do you enjoy sharing successes? We are a low ego group that promotes teamwork and collaboration to bring about success.

360 Degree Leader. We are a flat, non-hierarchical organization with a matrix structure that is dynamic and evolving. We expect you to be self-aware enough to recognize your position of unstated leadership within the company. You should have a demonstrated ability to lead and influence people through both formal and informal constructs and in situations where there is lack of clarity across teams. Finally, we need people who identify gaps and breakdowns and solve them immediately, rather than point them out and step back. You should also seek 360 feedback to help inform your growth trajectory as a leader.

Serve as the key bridge among internal Anduril departments—engineering, product, logistics, and more—to align efforts in developing and deploying integrated hardware-software C2 solutions that meet operational needs.

Champion the adoption of Connected Warfare products across Anduril divisions and into adjacent customer missions by identifying high-impact integration opportunities, building compelling internal use cases, and partnering with growth and engineering teams to expand the product footprint beyond initial deployments.

Facilitate Continuous Improvement:
Design and implement user feedback loops to systematically gather, prioritize, and share insights and challenges experienced by Anduril C2 products, ensuring that this valuable input drives collaborative enhancements.

Influence Product Evolution:
Actively engage with program and engineering teams to provide feedback that refines product features and optimizes user workflows, promoting a culture of shared excellence.

Build Strategic Internal Relationships:
Foster strong working relationships with program, engineering, and growth leaders across divisions, ensuring trust, clear communication, and alignment of goals to drive synergy and increased adoption of Anduril products.

Sales and Financial Metrics Tracking:
Navigate and utilize various internal business systems (e.g., ERP, CRM, BI tools) to accurately track, analyze, and report on product sales and key financial metrics.

- Secret/TS Clearance with SCI eligibility strongly preferred

We work within the IC to understand their requirements, shape their concepts of operation, and deliver exquisite capability across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers’ most pressing national security requirements.

ABOUT THE JOB

As an AIS Technical Program Manager, you will lead the development and/or integration of Anduril products and technologies with various government and industry partners. These projects will be diverse in nature and require you to be organized and flexible to adapt to changing situations. On one project, you may be working with the customer to clarify how each of its mission requirements can be met through Anduril's core products, including the plan, scope, and work required. In another situation, you may be helping to craft a vision with the customer or participating in technical working groups with a collaborative set of engineers to transform that vision into an operational reality. During all this, you must be able to successfully work with both external and internal stakeholders, communicate plans clearly to all parties, and support and coordinate across teams to achieve the desired end state.

Success in this position also hinges on two key facets: 1) systems and engineering mindset—the ability to understand and assess technical concepts—identifying system dependencies, interfaces, technical risks and the impact of key architectural decisions with the engineering team is a must; and 2) an execution mindset—digging into the details, charting the path and owning the outcome. You will be expected to utilize your technical aptitude in conjunction with your program and project management skills to deliver the best outcome for Anduril and the customer.

We are seeking a TPM with prior training and experience in a relevant engineering field to plan, direct, and lead internal and external program activities. The TPM will interact daily with the Chief Engineer to coordinate the execution of program initiatives and tasks—working alongside the rest of the team to meet the program’s administrative, technical, and operational requirements.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

In AIS, our TPMs are high-agency leaders who bridge the gap between complex engineering and mission execution. Operating at the intersection of hardware and software, TPMs do not just track tasks—they actively drive the development, testing, and deployment of cutting-edge technologies at insane speed.

Day in and day out, we expect our TPMs to act as force multipliers vice passive coordinators. - Proactively identify technical, supply chain, and schedule bottlenecks.

- Roll up their sleeves to help engineering teams unblock issues and make technical trade-offs.

- In conjunction with the Chief Engineer, anticipate single points of failure across technical architectures and critical path components; build proactive fallback options (e.g., drop-in hardware alternatives, modular software mocks) before risks materialize.

- Drive the contract deliverables process during the contract implementation period as well as during ongoing operations.

- Work with internal stakeholders and data management resources daily to ensure accurate development and timely submission of government deliverables, and ensure deliverables are contractually compliant, edited, approved, and submitted on time.

- Assist with the development of Forward-Looking Metrics and Trend Analysis to produce informative, easy-to-assimilate reports from the operational reporting systems, including written summary reports for Management.

- This reporting also allows them to define, plan, coordinate and conduct a comprehensive set of product and subsystem level reviews, change boards, and audits to manage change incorporation.

- Maintain schedule coherence and uniformity across multiple substantive teams, and multiple disconnected networks.

- Consulting with Program Managers and Engineering Leads to set up assignments, tasks, and subtasks.

- Developing, implementing, and maintaining an effective scheduling management system across one or more programs.

- Developing and coordinating an integrated master schedule (IMS) with internal departments and external stakeholders.

- Monitoring project timelines and deadlines.

- Identifying potential project schedule delays and facilitating intervention in a timely manner.

- Evaluating performance and preparing project progress reports based on schedule and cost performance.

- Accommodating updates and changes to project schedules.

- Recommending actions to keep projects within budget and completed on time.

- Keeping stakeholders informed of project timelines and deadlines.

- Work with proposal team to develop the IMS as needed.

- Documenting project scheduling processes and maintaining records.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor of Science degree in an engineering or related field.

- 8+ years of experience, specifically in technical project management, or related project management in a relevant industry.

- Ability to travel up to 20% as needed.

- Familiarity with government acquisition and reporting processes.

- Comfortable with contract financial data as it pertains to invoicing & analyzing staffing burn rates against contract ceilings.

- Ability to create and deliver presentations in technical and programmatic reports to key leadership and customers.

- Comfortable with setting and achieving goals in an amorphous environment.

- Adaptive and introspective; willing to learn, teach, lead and follow.

- Comfortable working in limited resource environments.

- Experience with government contracts strongly preferred.

- Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Domain expertise in the networking or telecommunications space.

- Prior experience developing end-device networking hardware.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. ABOUT THE TEAM

The Air Dominance and Strike Division is one of Anduril's fastest growing, most technically complex divisions. We develop and build collaborative combat aircraft, missiles, and the software that powers these autonomous weapons. We are scaling production of a first-of-kind autonomous aircraft at Arsenal 1 in Ohio, and quality is not just a compliance function here. It is a cost lever, a schedule lever, and a credibility lever with the customer.

ABOUT THE JOB

The system that connects incoming quality to defects to root cause to cost impact does not exist at scale yet. You are going to build it. You are not a quality engineer. You are the person who makes quality engineering outcomes measurable, sustainable, and tied to dollars.

Success in this position hinges on three key facets:

- Cost-of-Poor-Quality (COPQ) ownership - you own the financial narrative of quality. Every defect, every escape, every rework hour has a dollar value and you make that visible, traceable, and actionable.

- Cross-team accountability - when a defect pattern emerges, you trace it to the source, get the right people solving it, and prove it is fixed in cost and cycle time, not just defect count. Problems die at the root.

- Technical credibility - you understand manufacturing processes, materials, and failure modes well enough to challenge root cause analysis and know when a corrective action will actually hold.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Electronic Warfare (EW) division builds next-generation electronic warfare platforms — hardware-enabled, software-defined systems that are fielded, operational, and scaling fast. The EW team operates at a tempo the defense industry isn't used to: delivering novel system configurations into active operations in days, not months, securing major contract awards in under 24 hours, and earning unanimous fielding recommendations from government evaluators. Production is scaling from hundreds to thousands of units across multiple product variants, and the release and delivery challenges are scaling with it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Software Product Manager to own what ships to the operator. EW Mission Applications builds the software between the device and the operator — operator applications, Lattice integrations, shared visualization components, and the internal tooling that the rest of the business line runs on. You will own the roadmap for that surface: which capabilities reach operators, through which channel, and in what order.

EW Mission Applications delivers through multiple channels: each channel has different users, different timelines, and a different definition of done. Teams are organized by product surface rather than by program, so every engineering team supports several programs at once. Every program in the business line wants something from those teams. You decide what gets built, you write down why, and you hold that line when program pressure arrives — which it will, constantly, and for good reasons.

This role is product-focused and technically grounded. You won't write production code day to day, but you need to understand the device SDK boundary, the client architecture, and the integration surface well enough to tell a real blocker from a preference, to write requirements engineering can build against, and to negotiate scope with embedded engineering on the merits.

- Define operator capabilities before design and engineering start — the problem, the workflow, and the acceptance criteria that QA builds integration coverage against

- Deconflict competing program demands on shared engineering teams using a written, defensible prioritization framework

- Represent EW Mission Applications in the recurring device API review: bring the integration needs, justify the priority, agree the build order with embedded engineering, and track requests through to delivery

- Partner with UI design on operator workflows and with QA on test coverage, owning the requirement behind both

- Turn recurring field issues from our mission software engineering team into roadmap items and test coverage on a standing cadence

- Track delivery commitments against actuals and publish the results, so our estimates improve and our release commitments earn credibility

- Brief delivery status, roadmap changes, and risk to stakeholders at every level — engineers, program leadership, and customers — without flattening technical nuance into a status color

- Travel up to 25% to support integration events, deployments, field visits, and customer engagements

- Direct ownership of a product roadmap, including the authority and the track record to decline work

- Demonstrated ability to write requirements and acceptance criteria that engineering and test executed against

- Strong written and verbal communication skills — you'll be writing the roadmap, running prioritization calls, and briefing leadership

- Experience owning a software product surface that depended on hardware or firmware built by a team you did not control

- Experience deconflicting priorities across concurrent customers or programs competing for the same engineering capacity

- Ability to read and navigate codebases and API surfaces: you don't need to write production code, but you need to understand what is changing and what it costs

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Manufacturing Software
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build and deploy the technology stack that powers Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, the manufacturing execution system that workers and planners use every shift, the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that remove manual toil from the shop floor and business operations. MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology, incubating solutions close to the production line, validating them with real operators, hardening them for reliability and security, and scaling them across sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship. MDP is scaling from a founding team to more than 70 engineers across multiple U.S. sites, and you will be joining early to shape how manufacturing software is built at Anduril.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Staff Product Manager for Manufacturing Software, you will lead product for the entirety of Maritime Digital Production. Rather than owning a single line of effort, you will set product vision and strategy across MDP's domains: the factory data platform, the manufacturing execution applications, the scheduling and optimization engine, and the AI systems that remove manual toil from the shop floor and business operations. You will be the senior product voice for the function, balancing investment across these domains, raising the product bar, and guiding the other product managers on the team.

Product Leadership

You set the product bar for the entire function. You mentor and guide other product managers, establish the product practices and standards the team works to, and create clarity across domains so that individual owners can move fast without losing the thread of the broader strategy. You lead through influence rather than authority, earning trust with engineering, operations, and leadership across MDP.

Product Strategy

You can “see around the corner” for the function, crafting the vision, portfolio roadmap, and critical dependencies well beyond the current cycle. You constantly engage with stakeholders and leadership to solicit input and buy-in, proactively communicating goals and managing expectations. You escalate and own the largest tradeoffs and decision points across the portfolio.

Product Prioritization

You work backward from strategy to set clear outcomes across domains in partnership with your engineering, design, and operations leaders. You build the structures that let multiple teams prioritize competing work within rapid development cycles, and you keep the portfolio adaptable as new information arrives.

Problem Discovery and Solution Generation

You become attached to problems, not solutions. You seek out real-world context through onsite user research on the factory floor, direct conversations with technicians and operators, internal expert feedback, existing product data, and industry investigation. You separate what a customer asks for from what a customer actually needs, capture core workflows, and translate them into well-scoped requirements and success hypotheses across the portfolio.

Product Execution

From design to delivery, you fill gaps wherever needed to make well-scoped solutions a reality across the function. You proactively communicate with teams and leadership, approach solutions with humility and creativity to hit milestones, and set a high bar for how products are deployed, adopted, and supported on the floor.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Setting product vision and multi-year strategy across all of Maritime Digital Production, and making the portfolio-level tradeoffs about where the function invests across its domains

- Owning the cross-domain roadmap and prioritization, resolving competing demands between factory data, manufacturing execution, scheduling and optimization, and AI initiatives

- Gathering and refining both functional requirements and non-functional requirements such as tool capacity, performance, and reliability, and setting the standard for how requirements are captured and prioritized across the team

- Communicating across stakeholders and senior leadership, and exercising the judgment to tell whether a stakeholder truly needs what they are asking for or whether the underlying problem is better solved another way

- Walking the factory floor, talking directly with technicians and operators about how their work is going, and turning what you hear into opportunities to fix and improve the products across the portfolio

- Navigating the organizational dynamics between Maritime Digital Production and partner platform teams, advocating from the customer point of view when Maritime's needs differ from how a platform team would prefer to build

- Aligning and collaborating with the Corporate Technology product organization, keeping the Maritime product roadmap in sync with and aware of the broader CorpTech product roadmap so the two organizations move in step on shared platforms, standards, and dependencies

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 12+ years in a software product management role or similar leading role in product development, including experience owning a portfolio or leading product across multiple teams or domains

- Demonstrated ability to set product vision and strategy at a functional or organizational level and drive it through multiple teams

- Experience mentoring or guiding other product managers and establishing product practices and standards

- Domain expertise within hardware-related industries such as manufacturing, supply chain, warehousing, or logistics

- Demonstrated ability to gather and refine both functional and non-functional requirements (such as capacity, performance, and reliability) and turn them into a prioritized backlog

- Strong understanding of the interplay between enterprise systems, including ERP, WMS, MES, PLM, and supplier portals

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence engineers, operations stakeholders, and senior leadership, and to judge whether a request reflects a real underlying need

- Demonstrated success working directly with end users in operational environments, including time spent on a production or factory floor observing workflows firsthand

- Ability to navigate cross-team and cross-department dynamics, representing the customer point of view and building alignment when priorities differ

- Experience aligning a product roadmap with a partner or platform organization, keeping priorities in sync across groups that share technology and dependencies

- Demonstrated success decomposing complex problems into addressable component parts and arranging the correct sequencing across teams

- Proven ability to “see around corners” by crafting product strategy well beyond the current development cycle

- Comfort maturing products from MVP to enterprise-grade production at scale

- Must be able to travel up to 25% of the time

- U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export controlled data

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience building or owning manufacturing execution systems (MES), shop floor control systems, or operational software for factory, warehouse, or field environments

- Hands-on experience in manufacturing industries with time spent on assembly lines or in production facilities working directly with operators and technicians

- Experience with UI / UX web design tools (e.g. Figma)

- Familiarity with frontier AI tooling and AI-assisted software development workflows

- Experience in hyper-growth startup-like environments, balancing speed, ambiguity, and long-term platform health

- Background in operations research, industrial engineering, lean manufacturing, or continuous improvement methodologies

- Experience leading product across multiple domains or lines of effort within a single function or organization

- Experience supporting multi-site product rollouts, change management, and user training programs

We are not a traditional internal IT organization. We build, buy, customize, integrate, and operate the systems that make Anduril's physical operations faster, more reliable, and more scalable.

ABOUT THE JOB:

We are hiring a Staff Product Manager for Sustainment Solutions to own the digital portfolio that keeps Anduril's fielded systems mission-ready: operations planning, fleet management, maintenance execution, and customer support. This role turns a rapidly scaling, high-complexity sustainment mission into a durable operating advantage. You will own the roadmap, operating model, stakeholder relationships, and execution strategy for systems including our sustainment planning engine, fleet management and reliability tooling (asset tracking and FRACAS), field maintenance execution, and the customer service desk and portal. The role is not to "own the CMMS" or "run the service desk." The role is to help field maintainers, planners, fleet managers, supply chain, and the business lines win by building the right digital workflows across all of those

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

- Own the sustainment systems strategy and roadmap across operations planning, fleet management, maintenance execution, reliability / FRACAS, customer support, and more.

- Lead and grow the cross-functional team that delivers, operates, and improves these systems: product managers, software engineers, application engineers, and embedded builders from across the sustainment org.

- Partner deeply with field operations, maintainers, ProdOps, supply chain, engineering, and the business lines to understand the real constraints and build the workflow, not just the stated request.

- Create durable mechanisms for intake, prioritization, roadmap management, and stakeholder alignment without turning the org into a slow process machine.

- Drive tooling standardization across business lines where applicable, while enabling other business lines to succeed if they diverge from standard tooling and build their own to suit their use cases

- Translate messy field problems into clear system designs, phased execution plans, and measurable readiness outcomes.

- Advance our two expansion bets: the engineering feedback loop (turning field and FRACAS data into design change), and sparing / inventory for mission readiness as Anduril’s sustainment business scales into full MRO.

- Treat data quality, system reliability, integration design, access controls, auditability, and support models as first-class product requirements.

- Use AI, automation, and workflow redesign to cut manual coordination and make maintainers, planners, and support teams dramatically more effective.

- Planners and fleet managers have a single, trusted view of what is down, what is at risk, what is constrained, and what decision comes next.

- Maintenance execution in the field is structured, connected, and works in the offline and classified environments where most maintenance actually happens.

- Field and failure data flows back into engineering, so design changes are informed by what breaks and get operationalized into the fleet.

- Sparing and inventory stop being the bottleneck to readiness.

- Sustainment systems are connected end to end, so an incident can travel from detection through diagnosis, planning, execution, and closure without leaving the platform.

- The team is known for measurable readiness and cost impact, not just launches, tickets closed, or uptime.

- 7+ years working in and leading technology teams supporting complex physical operations such as maintenance, field service, fleet management, logistics, manufacturing, warehousing, etc.

- Strong understanding of one or more of: maintenance and reliability, fleet or asset management, sustainment planning, spares and inventory planning, or field service operations.

- A track record of cross-functional operational problems where the answer required more than one system, team, or process change.

- Strong product judgment: you can tell a local workaround from a durable platform capability, and you know when to ship the pragmatic version now versus invest in the scalable version later.

- High agency. You do not wait for someone to clarify every dependency or hand you a perfect roadmap.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Sand Table team at Anduril develops our revolutionary platform for visualizing future defense scenarios. We transform massive amounts of data into an intuitive, interactive 3D command center, serving as the visual interface for mission simulations, a key business development tool, and a powerful demonstration of our advanced capabilities to government and military leaders. We take ambitious ideas from concept to completion, building the core with high-performance C++ and enabling rapid feature expansion through modern scripting and plugin frameworks. The Sand Table team manages the complex logistics for delivering flawless augmented reality demonstrations in headset to critical stakeholders. As a cross-functional group of builders, strategists, and operators, we combine the creative energy of a top game studio with the rigorous discipline of national security to shape how the future of defense is visualized and understood.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to own execution for the Sand Table team—someone who will maintain our timelines, resolve dependencies, and keep everything on the rails towards final delivery. This is a high-agency role for someone who moves on things before being asked, anticipates problems before they materialize, and drives relentlessly toward outcomes. You will be the connective tissue between design, engineering, product, and key stakeholders, ensuring that our team ships high-quality, consistent releases on cadence while protecting the team's focus and momentum.

You'll manage the full complexity of delivering a real-time 3D platform that spans C++ engine development, XR hardware integration, plugin frameworks, and live demonstrations to senior government and military leaders. This means coordinating across technical work-streams, managing the logistics of high-stakes demos, and ensuring that every release meets the bar our audience demands. You should be comfortable navigating ambiguity, operating with minimal direction, and building the processes and structures that allow a fast-moving team to scale without losing speed.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Roll up their sleeves to help engineering teams unblock issues and make technical trade-offs.

- Drive the contract deliverables process during the contract implementation period as well as during ongoing operations.

- Work with internal stakeholders and data management resources daily to ensure accurate development and timely submission of government deliverables, and ensure deliverables are contractually compliant, edited, approved, and submitted on time.

- This reporting also allows them to define, plan, coordinate and conduct a comprehensive set of product and subsystem level reviews, change boards, and audits to manage change incorporation.

- Consulting with Program Managers and Engineering Leads to set up assignments, tasks, and subtasks.

- Identifying potential project schedule delays and facilitating intervention in a timely manner.

- Evaluating performance and preparing project progress reports based on schedule and cost performance.

- Accommodating updates and changes to project schedules.

- Recommending actions to keep projects within budget and completed on time.

- Keeping stakeholders informed of project timelines and deadlines.

- Work with proposal team to develop the IMS as needed.

- Documenting project scheduling processes and maintaining records.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 12+ years of experience, specifically in technical project management, or related project management in a relevant industry.

- Comfortable working in limited resource environments.

- Experience with government contracts strongly preferred.

- Must be able to work independently and as part of a multi-disciplinary team to deliver results in a highly ambiguous, fast-paced environment with little to no oversight.

jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking a Technical Program Manager to join the Maneuver Dominance - Enabling Technology team in London. The Maneuver Dominance (MD) Team at Anduril develops aerial robotic systems designed to operate in large coordinated teams in concert with ground manoeuvre forces. Maneuver Dominance develops perception, autonomy, and command and control (C2) systems to solve some of the hardest problems facing our customers.

The Enabling Technology (ET) team builds the shared capabilities that MD's programmes depend on, including mission systems, perception, navigation, effectors, and operator interfaces, developing them ahead of programme and product need rather than in response to it. As the TPM for Enabling Technology in the UK, you will own capability areas end to end: shaping what gets funded, driving it through development, and transitioning it into the programmes that consume it. Much of this work is delivered jointly with our US teams on a shared baseline, while nationally controlled elements are developed in country.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Own a capability area end to end, covering charter, budget, scope, and roadmap, partnered with an Engineering Lead who serves as technical principal investigator

- Lead a cross-functional capability team of hardware, software, and systems engineers to deliver capability that exceeds customer expectations

- Build and defend annual internal R&D (IRAD) submissions: shape proposals, size efforts, and take them through senior leadership review, then hold each funded effort to its charter

- Define and enforce exit criteria for each effort so that capability transitions cleanly into receiving programme teams and runs in their pipelines, rather than demonstrating once and stalling

- Serve as the primary liaison between technical teams, programme stakeholders, and customers, and as the ET point of contact in the UK

- Partner deeply with engineering leaders to drive execution, unblock technical challenges, and accelerate cross-team and cross-site projects

- Develop a deep understanding of mission requirements and master the technical concepts needed to identify key dependencies, trade-offs, and risks, particularly at the interfaces between mission systems, sensors, effectors, and the platforms that carry them

- Coordinate and execute frequent test events, from hardware-in-the-loop simulation through to ground test and live flight demonstration on rotorcraft and uncrewed air systems

- Work jointly with US teams on a shared baseline while ensuring nationally controlled elements are developed and held in country, making the call early on which elements belong where

- Plan and integrate across system boundaries, holding schedule and interface commitments when parts of the work are not visible to the whole team

- Proactively identify technical, programmatic, export control, and security risks, develop mitigation plans, and drive issues to resolution before they become blockers

- Foster a culture of extreme ownership and a bias towards action within the team

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- BEng/BSc/MEng in Electrical, Computer, Aerospace, or Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent experience

- Demonstrated experience owning programme management or engineering delivery for sophisticated hardware and software systems

- Make decisions when they're needed: re-sequence work, commit dates and scope to stakeholders, and approve spend that's already funded.

- Be the front door for requests from local leadership, Anduril's business lines and our own teams, and keep them briefed on the initiatives they depend on with short written updates.

- Work at the technical level. Understand networks, identity and physical security well enough to question a design, spot a gap in a bill of materials, and explain the trade-offs to executives.

- Partner with teams across Anduril, including Strategic Real Estate, Business Operations, Finance, Security and Trade Compliance.

- Use your expertise and judgement to help design how we run programs: templates, metrics, reporting and retrospectives that make each new market quicker to stand up than the last one.

- Bring the same discipline to our internal initiatives, such as capability development, planning cycles and leadership reviews.

- 5+ years in technical program or project management, including running several concurrent projects as a program

- A track record of delivering technical programs, such as offices, data centres, networks or secure facilities, where physical works and IT have to come together

- Experience in a startup or scale-up, where you built the process as you went

- A fast learner. You don't need a defence background, but you'll need to get across security, compliance and new markets quickly

- Technical enough to hold your own with engineers and make sound decisions on your own, and experienced enough to know when to escalate

- You've written the plans and updates that engineers, vendors and executives worked from, often across time zones, and kept them accurate through delivery

- A degree in engineering, computer science, information systems or a related field, or equivalent experience

- Australian work rights

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Delivered portfolios of programs across multiple countries, or across multiple sites and states within Australia

- Citizenship of an AUKUS nation (Australia, United Kingdom or United States)

- A project or program management qualification, such as PMP, PRINCE2, MSP or AgilePM. Useful to have, but experience delivering programs counts for more

- Experience with building, leading and developing teams of engineers.

- Adaptive and introspective; willing to learn, teach, lead and follow.

- Comfortable with setting and achieving goals in an amorphous environment.

- Comfortable with working in limited resource environments.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Seabed Sentry team is responsible for Maritime Domain Awareness providing subsea autonomous sensing and communication across critical commercial and defense mission sets. You'll operate in a fast-paced environment where small empowered teams move with urgency to deliver cutting-edge maritime capabilities from concept to deployment in months, not years. We bias toward action, embrace ambiguity, and expect technical program managers to drive execution with minimal bureaucracy — because the mission and the warfighter can't wait.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril Industries is seeking our next Technical Program Manager to lead international deployment execution for a maritime undersea domain awareness program. This role sits at the intersection of engineering, program management, and customer delivery — you will own the end-to-end execution of international demonstrations and system deployments, from planning through on-site execution. You will be the connective tissue between product teams, engineering, operations, business development, and international customers. This is not a role where you manage from a distance — you will be in the details, in the room with the customer, and accountable for delivery. Our next Technical Program Manager is the person who is energized by complexity, who builds trust with customers through competence and follow-through, and seeks to put order to chaos.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Own planning, scheduling, and execution of international system deployments and demonstrations for undersea domain awareness capabilities

- Build and maintain program schedules in Jira, ensuring milestones, dependencies, and critical path items are current and visible to all stakeholders

- Develop and maintain milestone trackers, risk registers, and action item burndowns across multiple concurrent workstreams

- Drive technical alignment across hardware, software, and systems engineering teams to ensure deployment-ready configurations meet customer requirements

- Prepare and deliver technical briefings and program status reviews to international customers, senior leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders

- Coordinate logistics for international hardware shipments including export compliance, temporary import/permanent export documentation, and customs coordination

- Identify and manage risks and dependencies across engineering, supply chain, compliance, and operations — escalate early and with proposed mitigations

- Translate customer requirements into actionable engineering tasking and ensure product teams understand the operational context behind what they're building

- Keep Jira updated as the single source of truth for schedule status — ensure sprint planning, epic tracking, and program milestones reflect reality, not aspirations

- Drive alignment across stakeholders who don't always agree — get decisions made, documented, and executed

- Support contract amendment processes, milestone payment tracking, and deliverable acceptance with the customer

- Document product baselines, configuration states, and deployment readiness criteria in Confluence

- Operate as the single point of accountability for deployment readiness — if something isn't tracking, you own the recovery plan

- 5+ years of technical program management experience, preferably in defense, maritime, or aerospace

- Demonstrated ability to manage international customer engagements and deployments in high-stakes environments

- Strong technical foundation — able to go deep on systems architecture, integration challenges, and hardware/software trade-offs without relying on engineering to translate for you

- Experience building and presenting technical briefings to senior military and government stakeholders

- Track record of managing complex, multi-team schedules with interdependent milestones and hard deadlines

- Proficiency in Jira for program scheduling, sprint management, and milestone tracking — you treat the tool as a real-time reflection of program health, not an administrative chore

- Exceptional organizational skills — you are the person who tracks every action item, every dependency, every open risk, and doesn't let things fall through

- Comfort operating in ambiguity and high-pressure situations where the plan is changing and decisions have real consequences

- Experience with export control processes (ITAR/EAR) and international logistics

- Familiarity with DoD acquisition processes, contract structures (FFP, T&M, CPFF), and milestone-based deliverables

- Ability to travel internationally up to 25%-40%, including extended deployments for demonstrations

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

- Experience in undersea warfare, autonomous systems, or maritime ISR programs
